name: auto-fire-weapons
demonstrates: CYBERPUN-17-9's auto-fire/weapon layer as it is reachable from a running build. GameScene.startPlayer(at:) builds one Player (the auto-fire composition) the first time a run mounts PlayerNode, and GameScene.advanceMovementAndCamera drives playerCombat.update(...) every .gameplay frame with raccoonSpawnDirector.targetCandidates as this frame's targets. WHAT THESE FRAMES ARE REVIEWED FOR: (1) the WEAPON OVERLAY -- WeaponOverlayRenderer parents a sprite_player_weapons cell as a child of PlayerNode.body at construction, on the SAME 36x40 cell and anchor as the body and with no visibility gate on having a target, a kill or a level-up, so the player is carrying a drawn gun from the very first gameplay frame; at the shipped 1x magnification that is a small, high-contrast detail composited on a 36x40pt body, not a separate on-screen object, so review it by zooming into the player rather than scanning the whole frame. (2) by the second screenshot the swarm has closed to RaccoonSeekBehavior.contactStandoffPoints (~17 points, i.e. well inside WeaponTier.handgun.rangeTiles = 5 tiles = 480 screen points), which is auto-fire's target precondition: raccoons ARE in weapon range in that frame. Timing is taken from the raccoon-swarm journey's already-captured evidence, which is the measured basis for the 30s/50s waits: RaccoonSpawnDirector.initialSpawnInterval is 3s and a spawn lands at least ~1,056 points off-screen (farAxisMinimumTiles) and then walks in. WHAT THESE FRAMES CANNOT SHOW, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A REGRESSION: no bullet, muzzle flash or hit puff can appear in a probe-driven run. AC1 makes MOVEMENT the fire gate -- WeaponFiringController.update(...) only fires while isMoving is true, which GameScene feeds from PlayerMovementController.isMoving, which is exactly StickState.isBeyondDeadZone. The probe's iOS step vocabulary (wait / screenshot / assert_running / navigate / tap_at / wait_for_element) has no press-drag-release verb, so nothing here can deflect the floating thumbstick past its dead zone: the player stands still for the whole run and auto-fire is suppressed BY DESIGN, exactly as AC1 requires ('standing still stops fire'). A tap_at step in the left half would only create the stick at zero deflection and release it, so no such step is included -- it would add a frame that still shows no bullets while implying movement was attempted. A reviewer who sees no bullets in these frames must read that as this probe-vocabulary limitation, NOT as 'auto-fire was not delivered'. The firing loop itself is pinned in-process, against the live scene rather than a double, by PlayerCombatSceneWiringTests (drives scene.playerCombat through GameScene and asserts a fired bullet's SCENE-space position lands on the shooter, the bullet is released back to the pool when its target despawns, and the overlay is a child of the mounted player's own body) and WeaponFiringControllerIntegrationTests (fire -> travel -> damage -> kill -> XP -> tier/overlay swap in the same frame), plus WeaponFiringControllerTests, TargetSelectionTests, BulletPoolTests, WeaponOverlayRendererTests, XPLevelSystemTests and RunStatsTests. TWO FURTHER ABSENCES THAT ARE NOT MISSES HERE: the muzzle flash is spawned at the player's actor anchor (his feet) rather than at the barrel tip, a recorded open AC6 gap awaiting a pixel measurement of sprite_player_weapons (see Player's 'Known gap' doc section) -- it is not visible in these frames anyway, for the movement reason above; and there is no XP/level/kill-count HUD, which is CYBERPUN-17-12's scope, not this story's. Gate is human/vision review of the two gameplay screenshots; assert_running steps only confirm the app process is still alive.

steps.target: the large neon-outlined PLAY button in the middle of the title screen that starts a new run (NOT the plain HIGH SCORES button below it)
steps.expect: the running game -- a playable isometric city scene with a ground lattice, buildings and a player actor, not a menu or title screen
